'''''Tower Belle''''' is a passenger boat based in [[Bristol Harbour]] in England. The vessel is operated by the [[Bristol Packet Boat Trips]], offering pleasure and educational trips through the City Docks and along  the River Avon to destinations such as  the Chequers Inn at [[Hanham Lock]] and Beese's Tea Gardens at [[Conham]]. '' Tower Belle'' was built in 1920 in [[Newcastle upon Tyne]] by [[Armstrong Whitworth]], originally known as ''Wincomblee''. In the 1950s and 1960s she worked in London, finally coming to Bristol in 1976.

==History==
Originally known as ''Wincomblee'' after a place in the [[Walker, Newcastle upon Tyne|Walker]] district of Newcastle, details of her early history are not known. She was operated by the Armstrong Whitworth company that built her, either as an executive launch or a company ferry for shipyard workers.<ref name=MNL01/> In 1939 she was transferred to [[Newcastle City Council]] and was likely used as a ferry on the [[River Tyne]] during the [[Second World War]]. In 1946 she was moved to London and then commenced passenger services on the [[River Thames]] from [[Westminster Pier]], downriver to [[Greenwich]] and up to [[Hampton Court]].<ref name="Bristol Post 01">{{cite news|last=Houseman|first=John|title=Sailing down memory lane on a tour around the harbour|url=http://www.lexisnexis.com/uk/nexis/results/docview/docview.do?docLinkInd=true&risb=21_T17924724586&format=GNBFI&sort=BOOLEAN&startDocNo=1&resultsUrlKey=29_T17924670749&cisb=22_T17924670748&treeMax=true&treeWidth=0&csi=166254&docNo=3|access-date=7 August 2013|newspaper=Bristol Post, archived at [[Lexis-Nexis]]|date=22 October 2012|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=NHRV>{{cite web|title=Tower Belle|url=http://www.nationalhistoricships.org.uk/register/333/tower-belle|work=National Register of Historic Vessels|publisher=National Historic Ships UK|access-date=7 August 2013}}</ref> A single [[Propeller (marine)|screw]] powered by diesel engine replaced the original steam powered twin screw arrangement. Her operators on the Thames were H G Hastings (1947–45), Thames Launches (1955–59) and, renamed ''Tower Belle'', W R Witham (1960–76).<ref>{{cite web|title=Tower Belle|url=http://riverthames.sosugary.com/displayimage.php?album=3&pid=1169#top_display_media|work=The Liquid Highway|access-date=7 August 2013}}</ref>

In 1976 she was abandoned, no longer considered river-worthy, at [[Eel Pie Island]] in [[Twickenham]]. There she was found by the owner of the Bristol Packet Boat Trips company, which operated narrowboat harbour tours in [[Bristol Harbour|Bristol City Docks]]. ''Tower Belle'' was brought by lorry to Bristol, sustaining further damage en route. After repairs she was re-launched into the docks in late 1976. Trips down the [[Avon Gorge]], to [[Avonmouth]] and back were offered, in addition to journeys upriver to the Chequers Inn at Hanham and Beese's Tea Gardens. Private parties, sometimes with an on-board jazz band were also offered.<ref name=NHRV/> In subsequent years, improvements to the vessel included the replacement of the wooden flooring with a more durable steel deck, and the addition of an electrical generator, enabling power for DJ parties and refrigeration for refreshments.<ref name=SB01>{{cite web|last=Staff|title=Tower Power|url=http://www.shipshapebristol.co.uk/2012/03/tower-power/|work=Shipshape Bristol|publisher=The Group of Seven|access-date=7 August 2013}}</ref><ref name=BP03>{{cite news|last=Staff|title=Harbour pleasure boat gets makeover|url=http://www.lexisnexis.com/uk/nexis/cart/cartDocRenderer.do?format=GNBFULL&returnToKey=20_T17925225708&randomNo=0.5948577150415936&csi=166254&docNo=1|access-date=7 August 2013|newspaper=Bristol Post at [[Lexis-Nexis]]|date=14 March 2006|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 2010, the 90th birthday of ''Tower Belle'' was celebrated with a special commemorative cruise which included the attendance of [[History of local government in Bristol#Mayors|Lord Mayor]] Colin Smith, who cut a cake and said, "It is remarkable that this boat can still be around after 90 years and, with the renaissance in the city docks, that boats such as this have come back into huge popularity and add to the city's culture."<ref name=BP02>{{cite news|title=Night-time party boat The Tower Belle marks 90th birthday|url=http://www.thisisbristol.co.uk/Night-time-party-boat-marks-90th-birthday/story-11255210-detail/story.html#axzz2bGg1BsAK|access-date=7 August 2013|newspaper=Bristol Post|date=30 September 2010}}</ref>

==Technical information==
''Tower Belle'' is powered by a diesel engine which drives a single propeller. Her overall length is {{Convert|67.97|ft|m|abbr=on}} and her beam is {{Convert|13|ft|m|abbr=on}}. The draught is {{Convert|2.83|ft|m|abbr=on}} and the air draught is {{Convert|12|ft|m|abbr=on}}. The ship is licensed to carry 95 passengers and is equipped with life rings, inflatable life rafts and life jackets. There is a small bar and toilet facilities.
